content: Auranofin is a medication prescribed to treat rheumatoid arthritis. It is used in combination with rest and non-drug therapies to alleviate symptoms such as painful, tender, or swollen joints and morning stiffness. In some cases, it may also be prescribed for other conditions. If you have questions about its use for other purposes, consult your doctor or pharmacist. Auranofin is available in capsule form and is taken orally, typically once or twice daily. It is essential to take this medication on a consistent schedule as directed by your doctor to achieve its full therapeutic effect. The benefits of auranofin may not become apparent for 3 to 4 months, and in some individuals, it may take up to 6 months. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and ask your doctor or pharmacist if you need clarification. Do not take more or less of the medication or take it more frequently than prescribed. In addition to rheumatoid arthritis, auranofin is sometimes used to treat psoriatic arthritis. If you are considering this medication for such purposes, discuss the potential risks with your doctor. Before starting auranofin, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to this medication or any other drugs. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are taking, especially arthritis medications, phenytoin (Dilantin), and vitamins. Notify your doctor if you have a history of heart, kidney, or liver disease; diabetes; bleeding disorders; inflammatory bowel disease; colitis; rashes; eczema; systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE); or bone marrow suppression. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking auranofin, contact your doctor immediately. Avoid attempting to conceive while on this medication and for at least six months after discontinuing it, as it remains in the body for an extended period. If you are scheduled for surgery, including dental procedures, inform your healthcare provider that you are taking auranofin. Refrain from consuming alcohol while on this medication. Auranofin may cause stomach upset. To minimize this, take the medication after meals or with a light snack. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Auranofin may cause side effects. Minor side effects include a metallic taste, loose stools or diarrhea, stomach pain, upset stomach, vomiting, gas, and hair loss. If these symptoms are severe or persistent, inform your doctor. Severe side effects require immediate medical attention. These include bloody or tarry stools, itching, skin rash, sore throat, mouth sores, fever, chills, unusual bruising or bleeding, blood in the urine, and fatigue. If you experience any of these, contact your doctor immediately. Serious side effects can also be reported to the FDA's MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program. Store auranofin in its original container, tightly sealed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture, and do not store it in the bathroom. Dispose of expired or unused medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance on disposal. In the event of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Attend all scheduled appointments with your doctor and laboratory, as regular monitoring is necessary to evaluate your response to auranofin. If you undergo a tuberculin (TB) skin test, inform the healthcare provider that you are taking auranofin. Do not share this medication with others, and consult your pharmacist if you have questions about refilling your prescription. Auranofin is sold under the brand name Ridaura®.
